notes: Region pack for central India's tiger forests and dry woodland: Madhya Pradesh (Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench, Satpura, Panna), Tadoba and Melghat in Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, the Deccan scrub around Nagpur and Hyderabad, the Chambal river and the dry plains and grassland of the region. Hand-picked on top of the India trip, which already holds most birds of the tiger forests (Brown Fish-Owl, Jungle Owlet, Indian Pitta, Grey-headed Fish-Eagle, Crested Serpent-Eagle, Changeable Hawk-Eagle, Sirkeer Malkoha, Yellow-footed Green-Pigeon, Indian Grey Hornbill, Common Woodshrike and the minivets). This pack adds 61 birds: owls and nightjars (Mottled Wood-Owl, Forest Owlet, Collared Scops Owl), the dry-country gamebirds (Painted Francolin, Painted Spurfowl, Rock and Painted Bush-Quail), the plains birds (Indian Courser, Painted and Chestnut-bellied Sandgrouse, Lesser Florican), Chambal river birds (Indian Skimmer, Black-bellied Tern), woodpeckers, Indian Nuthatch and Indian Spotted Creeper, Maroon Oriole, forest thrushes and winter flycatchers, scrub bulbuls and babblers, bushlarks, Green Avadavat and Crested Bunting. Ranked by GBIF/eBird counts for the whole of India (in/occurrence.csv) plus birding knowledge; vagrants and expedition-only birds left out. Several birds fit other packs as well and are kept here on purpose, to be settled centrally: Yellow-billed Babbler, White-browed Bulbul, Yellow-throated Bulbul, Tawny-bellied Babbler, Painted Spurfowl, Rock and Painted Bush-Quail and Tawny Lark (Western Ghats and the far south or the dry west), Chestnut-bellied Sandgrouse and Indian Skimmer (Thar and Gujarat), Lesser Florican (grasslands of the west), and the winter visitors White-throated Fantail, Grey-headed Canary-Flycatcher, Ultramarine Flycatcher, Chestnut-bellied Rock Thrush, Indian Blue Robin and Orange Minivet (Himalaya breeders, also met in the Ghats). Dropped for lack of trustworthy photos in the library (reviewed from contact sheets): Large-billed Leaf Warbler, Western Crowned Warbler, Tickell's Leaf Warbler, Thick-billed Warbler, Thick-billed Flowerpecker, Besra, Jerdon's Leafbird (cannot be told from Golden-fronted Leafbird), Bronzed Drongo, Grey-bellied Cuckoo, White-tailed Iora (photos look like Common Iora) and Singing Bushlark (photos mixed with Australasian Bushlark). Also tried and left out for photos or fit: Dollarbird (photos look Australian), Hair-crested Drongo, Pied Thrush, bitterns, Watercock, malkohas, Lesser Coucal, Short-eared Owl, Asian Barred Owlet, Asian Fairy-bluebird, White-rumped Shama, Eastern Orphean Warbler, Blue-throated Flycatcher. Left out on purpose as they sit in other packs: Great Indian Bustard, Sykes's Nightjar and desert larks (IN-DESERT), the Western Ghats endemics and Blue-faced Malkoha (IN-WESTERNGHATS). Left out earlier by the country trip because photos could not be identified, and not retried: Indian Scops Owl, Indian Spotted Eagle, Savanna Nightjar, Streak-throated Swallow. Forest Owlet is in with only five approved-quality photos (moderately sure). Shaky photo picks, to check on /trip-photos: Banded Bay Cuckoo, Plaintive Cuckoo, Rufous-fronted Prinia, Forest Owlet and Rock Bush-Quail (five photos each, sheets mixed with look-alikes), Jungle Nightjar, Jerdon's Nightjar, Collared Scops Owl, Lesser Fish-Eagle, Montagu's Harrier, Pied Harrier, Indian Cuckoo, Indian Nuthatch, Puff-throated Babbler, Large Woodshrike, Yellow-billed Babbler, Tawny Lark, Bengal and Indian Bushlark, Sulphur-bellied Warbler, Brown-breasted Flycatcher, Tickell's Thrush, Yellow-throated Bulbul, Painted Bush-Quail, Black-bellied Tern, Orange Minivet, European Bee-eater, Black-naped Oriole.
